question:
A 16-year-old Caucasian boy presents to your family practice office complaining of itchiness. He denies other symptoms. He also denies tobacco, alcohol, or other illicit drug use and is not sexually active. He has no other significant past medical or surgical history aside from a meniscal repair from a wrestling injury sustained two years ago from which he has recovered fully. Vitals are T 98.3, HR 67, BP 110/70. On exam you note several pruritic, erythematous, slightly raised annular patches with central clearing on his back.

Which of the following additional tests or features are sufficient to make the diagnosis of this boy's skin lesion?

options.opa: Acid-fast bacilli on smear from skin scrapings
options.opb: History of recent herald patch and lesions along skin cleavage lines
options.opc: Presence of hyphae when KOH added to skin scrapings
options.opd: Symmetrical distribution on bilaterial extremities progressing proximally
options.ope: History of time spent in a Lyme-endemic region

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Pruritic, erythematous, annular patches with central clearing" -> "suggestive of tinea corporis" -> "KOH preparation shows hyphae" -> "diagnosis of tinea confirmed" -> 95%

CHAIN: "Pruritic, erythematous, annular patches with central clearing" -> "possible diagnosis of pityriasis rosea" -> "history of recent herald patch" -> "diagnosis of pityriasis rosea confirmed" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Pruritic, erythematous, annular patches with central clearing" -> "symmetrical distribution on bilateral extremities" -> "possible diagnosis of eczema or psoriasis" -> "requires further evaluation" -> 70%

CHAIN: "Pruritic, erythematous, annular patches with central clearing" -> "history of time spent in a Lyme-endemic region" -> "possible Lyme disease-related rash" -> "requires serological testing for confirmation" -> 60%

CHAIN: "Pruritic, erythematous, annular patches with central clearing" -> "acid-fast bacilli on smear from skin scrapings" -> "suggests possible mycobacterial infection" -> "not typical for presented lesions" -> "unlikely diagnosis" -> 40%
analysis: The clinical presentation of pruritic, erythematous, slightly raised annular patches with central clearing is characteristic of tinea corporis (ringworm). The presence of hyphae when KOH is added to skin scrapings would confirm the diagnosis by identifying the fungal elements responsible for the infection. Other options do not align with the typical presentation of tinea corporis.
